newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Amcor says plans European, U.S. expansion.
newsitem.headline: Amcor says plans European, U.S. expansion.

text.p: Amcor Ltd managing director Don Macfarlane said in a newspaper interview that the paper and packaging group planned to spend about A$200 million on acquisitions in the United States and Europe.
"We are looking very carefully at opportunities, first in Euorpe and secondly in North Americia, for operations of a signficant size," Macfarlane told the Tuesday edition of The Australian newspaper.
Amcor was looking for purchases of the scale of the May 1996 A$200 million purchase of the Belgian-based UCB Flexibles packaging business, he said.
Macfarlane said Amcor was in a good position to borrow, given its US$230 million convertible subordinated note issue late last year, which gave Amcor a 42 percent debt to shareholders funds ratio.
This compares with a self-imposed limit of 67 percent.
Macfarlane said the first priority was a European purchase, probably in flexible packaging or bottle tops.
The expansion programme would also include smaller purchases of non-paper product makers or corrugated box makers in Eastern Europe.
"Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary seem to be the best prospects for business in general," Macfarlane said.
He said Amcor was not interested in a big purchase in Asia, where the company already has five percent of its assets.
"I can see five percent going to 10 percent, but we're not about to dash into that part of the world with a big investment," he said.
Amcor's shares closed down two cents at A$8.12 on Monday.
